findings.title: The reparse-point (junction/symlink) check that the PR describes is not implemented.
findings.body: The PR's security table says each component of the resolved path is rejected if it has `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint`. Neither `TryGetLocalImageVirtualUrl` nor `TryResolveVirtualUrl`, nor the serving code in the control, checks attributes. Containment is purely lexical. A cloned repo or extracted folder that has a symlink or junction such as `images -> C:\Users\<user>\Pictures` passes the check, and the handler reads files outside the allowed tree. Fix: add the per-component reparse-point check before serving, or correct the documented security model.

findings.title: Raw HTML `src` is only sanitized when local images are on, and `srcset` is never removed, contrary to the stated security model.
findings.body: The PR says raw HTML `src` is rewritten to `#` with the setting OFF too, so `data:` images cannot render, and that `srcset` is removed in both states. The rewrite is wrapped in `if (allowLocalImages)`, so with the default OFF state `` still renders. No code touches `srcset` in either state. The regex also matches only double-quoted `src`. With the setting ON, `src='data:...'` or an unquoted `src` passes through unchanged and does not fire the blocked-image callback. Fix: run the sanitizer in both states (blocking everything when OFF), strip `srcset`, and handle single-quoted and unquoted attributes. Alternatively, sanitize the Markdig HtmlBlock/HtmlInline nodes instead of using a regex.

findings.title: Local images in raw HTML with single-quoted or unquoted `src` are never rendered.
findings.body: The pattern only matches `src="..."`. With the setting enabled, `` or `` is left untouched. The browser then requests a `file:` or relative URL, which the resource filter answers with 403. The image stays blocked and the info bar does not appear. Fix: extend the pattern to accept `'...'` and unquoted values, or rewrite the attributes on the parsed HTML nodes.

findings.title: The share-root logic widens the allowed base for `\\?\` and `\\.\` paths and admin shares.
findings.body: Any directory that starts with `\\` is treated as UNC, and the first two path segments become `_allowedBasePath`. If the file arrives as a long or device path, the base becomes far too broad. `\\?\C:\docs\x` gives the base `\\?\C:` (the whole drive), and `\\?\UNC\server\share\x` gives `\\?\UNC`. A `\\server\C$\...` path also gives the whole remote drive. Containment is then checked against that base, on both the rewrite side and the serving side, so `../../..` references can reach far outside the document folder. I could not confirm whether Explorer ever passes `\\?\` paths to this handler. Fix: parse the path with a real UNC/device-path parser and handle the `\\?\UNC\` and `\\?\X:` forms. Otherwise fall back to the markdown directory rather than an inferred root.

findings.title: Image files are read whole and synchronously on the UI thread, with no size or type limit.
findings.body: `WebResourceRequested` runs on the UI thread. `File.ReadAllBytes` loads the entire file, which can be slow on a network share. The serving side also accepts any file under the base, not just images. A document that references something like `![](big.iso)`, or several large files on a slow UNC share, freezes the preview pane and can throw `OutOfMemoryException`, which is not caught here. Fix: use `GetDeferral()` with a `FileStream` opened asynchronously, cap the file size, and serve only image extensions.

held.title: Settings read failures other than a missing file break the whole Markdown preview.
held.body: Only `FileNotFoundException` is caught. A settings.json that is corrupt or locked, or a missing directory, makes `GetSettings` throw `JsonException`, `IOException` or `DirectoryNotFoundException`. Because `GetLocalImagesEnabled` is called inside `DoPreview` before rendering, the whole preview then fails instead of just falling back to blocking images. I could not see how `SettingsUtils.GetSettings` handles these errors internally. Fix: catch `Exception` (or use `GetSettingsOrDefault`) and return false.
